outcome: A modal triggered ability with no mode chosen is removed from the stack without resolving.
A mode chosen multiple times is carried out that many times in sequence on resolution.
Redirecting a modal spell's target leaves its chosen mode unchanged.
A copy of a modal spell or ability resolves with the same modes as the original.
A modal spell with a costed mode shows a higher cost after adjustment when that mode is chosen.
Cards split into piles stay in their zone until the effect moves them.
A devotion-based static ability turns a permanent on or off according to the count of matching mana symbols among the controller's permanents.
Devotion is computed after copy, control and text-changing effects but before other characteristic changes, so a god's own type change does not alter the count.
A delayed effect that says 'this [something]' still acts on the original object even if it no longer has that quality.
A party-counting effect yields a number from zero to four computed automatically.
A multi-type creature counts as a member of only one party slot, chosen to maximise the party size.
A condition on a permanent that was activated this turn holds if it was the source of an activated ability this turn, even if it lost the ability.
A player has descended if a permanent card was put into their graveyard from anywhere this turn, even if it has since left.
Effects that refer to outlaws count only outlaw permanents unless otherwise specified.

A crime is committed, and crime triggers fire, when a spell or ability is cast, activated or put on the stack targeting an opponent, an opponent's permanent, spell or ability, or a card in an opponent's graveyard.
An expend trigger fires when mana spent on spells this turn crosses the threshold N as a cost is paid.
A worthy-creature effect applies to a creature only if it is legendary, not a Villain, and red or white.
